part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `parseFunctionBody` (packages/babel-parser/src/parser/expression.js:2600): when a function had a concise expression body (e.g. the arrow `()=>null`), the parser pushed an `ExpressionScope` onto the expression-scope stack but never popped it — the block-body branch did (`exit()` at line 2676), the expression-body branch didn't.

For `function f(_=()=>null) {}`, the leaked scope shifted the stack so the `expressionScope.exit()` in `parseFunctionParams` popped the wrong scope, leaving the `ParameterDeclaration` scope active. The following `await`/`yield` in the enclosing async/generator function then hit `recordParameterInitializerError` and was incorrectly rejected with "'await' is not allowed in async function parameters" / "Yield expression is not allowed in formal parameters".

The fix is a one-liner — `this.expressionScope.exit();` after parsing an expression body. Verified:
- Both issue repros now parse
- Genuine `await`/`yield`-in-params errors (`function f(a = await b) {}`, `(a = await b) => {}`, async arrow heads, etc.) are still raised correctly
- Full `babel-parser` suite: 10737 passed; dependent packages (`babel-core`, `babel-generator`, `babel-template`, `babel-types`, `babel-traverse`) pass except 4 failures that also fail on the unmodified baseline
